units.account: Col. Aubry did exactly as ordered. He wheeled his right companies towards the bridge and gave rolling volleys into the column as soon as its head set foot on the span. Some of the leading enemy reached his front with the bayonet and were thrown back. He held his ground throughout.

Col. Delacroix held his line beside the 1st and turned his left wing on the bridge, firing into the flank of the column as it crowded the far end of the span. He did not advance a step beyond his line.

Maj. Verneuil had no orders, but he saw the enemy column stall in disorder at the bridge exit under the crossfire and charged its head on his own initiative. He drove it back onto the span. Then he reined in at the bridge rather than cross under the guns of the far bank, and re-formed behind the infantry.
units.departure: The engine had the squadron cross the bridge and chase the broken battalion more than a kilometre to (2000,348). It charged the column's head at the bridge exit, stopped at the river and re-formed behind its own line.

units.account: Col. Brandt flung his column at the bridge at the double with bayonets fixed, forbidding any firing. The head crossed the span under a crossfire from two lines. A few companies reached the south bank, but there the column stalled, and a charge of horse threw it back onto the bridge. The battalion broke and streamed back across the river and up the road, Brandt trying in vain to stop it.
units.departure: The engine had the battalion broken and butchered down to 96 men, back at (1950,300) by minute 17. Crossfire and one charge at the bridge plausibly cost about 180 men. The fugitives are about 600 m up the road by turn's end, not 1.3 km away, and not cut down in a 1 km cavalry pursuit.

units.account: Col. Hartmann advanced his line to the edge of the north bank as ordered. The enemy battalions stood about 300 m beyond the river, too far for musketry, so he held his fire rather than waste powder. He watched the Vanguard's assault fail on the bridge.
Maj. von Reiter had no orders. He held his hussars west of the road and watched the assault fail. The river stopped him intervening.

summary: Turn 2 (20-40). Red's Vanguard Battalion stormed the bridge at the double in column, bayonets fixed and not firing. Blue's 1st and 2nd Battalions, in line about 80 m either side of the bridge's south exit, caught the column in a crossfire of volleys from minute 5. The head reached the south bank in disorder and some companies came to the bayonet against the 1st Battalion's right. Around minute 10, Blue's cavalry squadron charged on its own initiative and drove the stalled head back onto the span, and the battalion broke. It fled back over the bridge and up the high road. It lost about 180 men and ends broken around (2050,1050). The squadron stopped at the river and re-formed behind the Blue line, losing 14 men. Red's Line Battalion lined the north bank as ordered, but the Blue lines were about 300 m off, beyond musket range, so it held its fire. Red's hussars, without orders, stayed west of the road. Blue's infantry lost only a handful of men and spent part of its ammunition. Blue still holds the bridge and its south end. The engine's projection had the broken Vanguard chased 1.3 km and cut down to 96 men; that was rejected as implausible.
